answer: Each identity locks 50 credits and holds a unique data shard recorded in a quartz ledger. Auditors open a retrieval thread and ask the identity to echo back random bytes from its shard within a deadline; a missing or wrong echo burns the bond. A sybil operator must store a separate shard for every fake, so the k-th fake needs new disk space: 50 bond plus 30 storage rent, and 1000 fakes cost 80,000 credits. Rented storage fails: a shard copied to two identities returns the same echo for both, and both bonds burn. An honest agent locks 50 once and stores one shard.
